page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-32 is a compute-focused instance variant provisioned with an elevated memory footprint. Built on x86_64 architecture, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor running two threads per core. The processor allocation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates hardware acceleration flags for cryptographic tasks like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, alongside standard AVX extensions. The instance is allocated 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage devices or dedicated GPUs are bundled into this server tier, requiring external persistent network storage.

Empirical benchmark evaluation reflects strong memory and execution characteristics. The instance scored 3056.06 on the PassMark memory evaluation, placing it in the top 10 percent of recorded systems, supported by 127.51 GB/sec large-block uncached read bandwidth and 64.95 GB/sec write bandwidth. Single-core compute capability is solid, with a stress-ng score of 2927.79 in the top 25 percent and a PassMark encryption score of 37408.06 reflecting strong hardware cryptographic handling. Multi-core execution benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core at 14622.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 46953.76, remain strictly in the middle 50 percent range. In inference testing, generation using small and medium models maintained top-quartile speeds, though processing 70B parameter models dropped into the lower quartile.

Cost efficiency centers on density for memory-dependent processing where dedicated physical cores are unnecessary. Lacking local NVMe arrays, I/O performance relies fully on attached network block storage, creating an architectural dependency. The instance matches requirements for medium to large in-memory databases, Redis deployments, continuous integration compilation jobs, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine configured with an expansive memory ratio. Driven by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache, AES cryptography acceleration, and 256 GB of system RAM. Hardware evaluations highlight top-decile PassMark memory results alongside top-quartile cryptographic performance and single-core stress-ng benchmarks. Multi-threaded compilation and general compute metrics remain in the median tier. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local solid-state drives, directing all storage requirements to attached network volumes. Because of the 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation and strong memory bandwidth, the server functions effectively for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, batch data processing, and large-scale compilation tasks.
